subtype: Approach: paste the assignment and submit the result [Pitfall]
passage:
"Farida, sit down. Read this paragraph aloud for me."

"Professor Mridul, I—"

"Please."

"'The novel critiques colonial railway policy in the seventh chapter.'"

"There is no railway in the seventh chapter, and the book has no colonial chapter at all. Also, this quote does not appear anywhere in the text."

Farida's face went hot. "I ran out of time. I put the question into a tool and submitted what it gave me."

"The college rules say your submission must be your own work. You will need to write it again, with a note to the committee. You'll also lose the marks for this one."

"I know. I'm sorry. I didn't learn anything, did I?"

"Not from that one."

qa.q: What did the professor say was missing from the seventh chapter?
qa.a: There is no railway in the seventh chapter.

qa.q: What is Farida feeling as Farida's face goes hot?
qa.a: Farida feels embarrassed and regretful, having taken a shortcut under time pressure that has now cost marks.

qa.q: What could Farida do next time when short of time, and why?
qa.a: Farida could ask the professor for a short extension or submit a smaller honest draft, because an honest partial attempt teaches more than a polished copy.

qa.q: How might Professor Mridul see the submitted essay?
qa.a: Professor Mridul sees work with invented quotes that does not show what Farida understands, and is bound by the rules on originality.

grounding: Pressed for time, a student submits an AI-written essay unchanged, and the errors, policy breach and lack of learning cost more later.
